features.name: Show and lock orientation
features.note: All 5 controls present (structural parity 5/5, non-blank frame) and the page is reachable. But the sample's primary output is broken: UWP reports Native/Current orientation = 'Landscape' and Auto-rotation = 'None', while the migrated WinUI 3 app shows 'N/A' and a raw exception message ('DisplayInformation not available on desktop... GetForCurrentView must be called on a thread associated with a CoreWindow'). The migration used DisplayInformation.GetForCurrentView(), which throws on WinUI 3 desktop. The feature is non-functional though it degrades to a visible fallback, so it is partial, not pass. The 'Apply preferences' button was a no-op in both UWP and WinUI (0/1 live in each), so that alone is not a regression.
